national_raw_news.title: DGHS warns against reuse of single-use medical devices
national_raw_news.content: Director General of Health Services (DGHS) has warned against the reuse of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items in all public and private healthcare facilities. In a letter to Chief Secretaries, Health Secretaries and Directors of Heath Services of all States and UTs, DGHS said that it has come to its notice that certain private and corporate hospitals are reusing various single-use medical devices and disposable surgical Items, particularly in critical specialities such as Cardiology, Nephrology, Oncology, Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery, Neurosurgery, and other specialised clinical services. DGHS has observed that such devices and disposable surgical items, after being used for one procedure, are being subjected to sterilisation and subsequently reused, despite being designated for single use only. More from our correspondent: DGHS has said that the practice of reusing single-use devices and disposable surgical items raises concerns relating to patient safety, infection prevention and control, regulatory compliance, and healthcare expenditure. It has warned that this can also expose patients to significant risks, including cross-infection, device malfunction, loss of performance, and other procedure-related complications. DGHS has asked all States and Union Territories to ensure strict vigilance and effective enforcement against the reuse of single-use medical devices and disposable surgical items.

national_raw_news.title: India Chem 2026 concludes in Mumbai, highlighting India’s emergence as global chemicals hub
national_raw_news.content: The 14th edition of India Chem 2026 held under the theme “Advantage Bharat : An Emerging Global Chemicals Hub” concluded in Mumbai today. This event, organized jointly by the Department of Chemicals & Petrochemicals and FICCI, provided a platform for brainstorming discussions amongst industry leaders and government representatives on specific topics of relevance to the sector, facilitating dialogue on investment prospects, regulatory frameworks, and strategic challenges. Japan, with whom India shares a robust trade relationship, particularly in the chemical and petrochemical sector, was the partner country for the event. During the brainstorming sessions under India-Japan, India-US and India-EU Chemicals and Petrochemicals Forum, representatives and industry leaders explored opportunities for deeper collaboration in trade, investment and technology related to the sector. Meanwhile, roundtables were also held on themes like Specialty Chemicals, Infrastructure for Chemicals and Petrochemicals, Agrochemicals, Environment Issues, Plant Machinery, Pumps and Valves. The 14th edition also witnessed “India Chem Youth Innovation Challenge”, wherein young students had to work on problem statements provided by the chemical industry. According to an official statement, the First Prize was clinched by Soumya Bhole and Sarthak Kale of ICT, Mumbai. Suman Batwe and Saloni Mhadesar of VNIT, Nagpur and Jash Prasad and Smit Bambhorliya of IIT, Gandhinagar clinched second and third prizes respectively. The event, which witnessed a footfall of more than 5000 visitors across three days.

national_raw_news.title: Centre achieves target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs across the country
national_raw_news.content: The Centre has created 11 crore farmer IDs across the country, five months ahead of the March 2027 deadline. The milestone has been achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The Farmer ID initiative is designed to provide farmers with a unique digital identity, enabling transparent, efficient and timely access to government schemes, bank credit, crop insurance and disaster relief, while reducing paperwork and repeated verification. Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said this today while sharing a video message. The Minister said that the target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs by March 2027 was set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and it was achieved yesterday, five months ahead of schedule. Mr Chouhan said that Farmer IDs will ensure transparent delivery of benefits under various government schemes. They will facilitate farmers in accessing bank loans, crop insurance, disaster relief assistance and selling their produce. He added that the initiative will help ensure that benefits reach the right farmers, while the use of modern technology will make farming easier and more efficient. Mr Chouhan congratulated and thanked the officials and employees of the Central Government, as well as the state governments, union territories, and district administrations, for this achievement. The Ministry added that the Digital Agriculture Mission was launched following the Union Cabinet’s approval on 2nd September, 2024. The Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) being developed under the mission is already showing results on the ground. It added that through the Farmer ID-based service delivery system, more than 6 crore farmers across the country have so far received direct benefits under various schemes. Linking a verified farmer database with agricultural services is helping eliminate fraud and the need for duplicate verification. The Ministry furhter stated that it has also improved coordination among government departments and strengthened policy formulation and the monitoring of schemes, making it easier to track their implementation and delivery of benefits.

national_raw_news.title: Next wave of retail broking to come from towns, villages, says SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey 56 mins ago 34
national_raw_news.content: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey today said that the next wave in retail broking will not come from the big cities alone but will come from towns and villages. Addressing the 16th International Capital Market Convention of Association of NSE Members of India – ANMI, Mr. Pandey said, the best brokers do not just execute trades, they guide. Stating that KYC must be treated as “Know Your Client’s Needs”, SEBI Chairman said a client who understands risks invests wisely and stays invested longer. He further encouraged brokers to introduce investors to choices beyond equity like a bond, or a unit of a REIT or an InvIT. Raising serious concerns that about six in ten investors rely on unregistered advisers and so-called influencers, Mr. Pandey said SEBI’s campaign “Samajh Se Investing Simple” has drawn over 15 crore views on social media and sent close to 110 crore WhatsApp messages since its launch on 5th October. Urging market participants to treat cyber security as a business priority, not an IT expense, the SEBI chief said a single breach can shake trust across the system. Stating that the International Monetary Fund – IMF expects India to grow at about 7 percent this year, which is more than twice the global pace, Mr. Pandey said, the prediction is largely due to the country’s young population, large domestic market and steady reforms. He informed that India’s equity market capitalization stands around 470 lakh crore rupees while Mutual Fund Assets Under Management – AUM stand around 83 lakh crore rupees. With over 15 crore unique investors and a foreign portfolio investor assets of about 74 lakh crore rupees, Mr. Pandey said the aim is to keep building a market that is simpler, deeper and safer, for investors and for market participants. In that direction, the SEBI Chief said, the regulator is reviewing short selling and securities lending and borrowing to improve liquidity and price discovery. He added that a framework is being developed to lift secondary trading in corporate bonds and another to put in place safeguards to prevent misuse of trading terminals. Mr. Pandey said SEBI is also exploring an AI sandbox, where new tools can be tested safely.

national_raw_news.title: Benchmark indices snap two-week winning streak amid rising crude oil prices 5 hours ago 68
national_raw_news.content: Benchmark domestic indices snapped their two-week rising streak dragged by higher crude oil prices due to escalating West Asia conflict. During the holiday-shortened week, the 30-share Sensex at the Bombay Stock Exchange declined 1 thousand 605 points, or 2.14 per cent, to close at 73 thousand 124. The National Stock Exchange Nifty 50 lost 546 points, or 2.35 per cent to end at 22 thousand 600. The sell-off spread beyond large-cap stocks, with mid-cap and small-cap indices experiencing sharper declines as investors reduced exposure amid rising uncertainty. In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, Midcap 100 index shed 5.6 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 index tanked more than 7 percent during the week. Across sectors, IT was the lone pocket of resilience, recovering from early selling to end the week largely unchanged on improving earnings visibility and renewed investor appetite. Among the major laggards, Nifty Defence index plunged seven per cent, followed by the Nifty Consumer Durables index, which fell 6.4 per cent. Investors’ wealth eroded this week, with the total market capitalization of BSE listed companies declining by nearly 21 lakh crore rupees. In the forex market, the Indian rupee appreciated marginally this week to settle at 94 rupees and 94 paise against the US dollar.

national_raw_news.title: Govt to bear entire cost of expensive certification for micro and small enterprises under EPM
national_raw_news.content: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said the government is willing to bear the entire cost of expensive certifications for micro and small enterprises under the Export Promotion Mission, EPM, to help Indian businesses access global markets. Addressing reporters in Berlin on his two-day visit to Germany, Mr Goyal urged existing and prospective exporters to approach the Directorate General of Foreign Trade for assistance with certifications and regulatory compliance. He said the government would also support micro and small enterprises in meeting European Union requirements, including the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism and the EU Deforestation Regulation. Support for other businesses would be provided on a graded basis. The Export Promotion Mission, approved in November last year with an outlay of 25,060 crore rupees over six financial years, is being implemented through two sub-schemes: Niryat Protsahan, with an allocation of 10,401 crore rupees, and Niryat Disha, with 14,659 crore rupees. Mr Goyal also said German companies increasingly view India as a strategic hub for manufacturing, research and development, and innovation, in addition to being a major consumer market. During his visit, he held meetings with representatives of Siemens Healthcare, Bertelsmann Investment, Volkswagen and Skoda to discuss opportunities to strengthen trade and investment between the two countries. Highlighting the potential of closer cooperation, the Minister said German expertise in precision and research, combined with India’s skilled workforce and manufacturing capabilities, could strengthen India’s global position. He added that bilateral ties offer opportunities not only in trade in goods and services, but also in talent exchange, innovation, joint design, development and manufacturing. Around 2,000 German companies currently operate in India, reflecting the depth of industrial and commercial ties between the two countries.

national_raw_news.title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman Calls for Stronger Cybersecurity Amid Global Uncertainties
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has urged financial sector regulators and other stakeholders to expedite the refund of unclaimed assets to their rightful owners. These include bank deposits, dividends, shares, post office savings, insurance proceeds and pension funds. Ms Sitharaman stated this while chairing the 30th meeting of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) in New Delhi yesterday. Ms Sitharaman also called for simplifying Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures and strengthening cybersecurity preparedness amid rising geopolitical uncertainties. The Council reviewed efforts under the ‘Your Money, Your Right’ campaign, which aims to facilitate the return of unclaimed financial assets to their rightful owners. It urged the concerned ministries and regulators to intensify their efforts to ensure timely refunds. The Council also deliberated on issues relating to macroeconomic and financial stability, as well as the country’s preparedness to address emerging challenges. Discussions included measures to promote innovation in the fintech sector and explore the potential of tokenisation of financial assets and other real-world assets. According to the Finance Ministry, the meeting also reviewed the country’s preparedness to protect critical information infrastructure, strengthen the resilience of security systems and enhance cybersecurity preparedness among Regional Rural Banks. In view of growing geopolitical challenges and global uncertainties, the Finance Minister called for more frequent meetings of the Council according to a predefined schedule. The meeting was attended by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, Chief Economic Adviser Dr V. Anantha Nageswaran, Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology S. Krishnan, and other senior officials.

national_raw_news.title: SBI Assures Customers of Safe Funds After Suspected Data Breach
national_raw_news.content: The State Bank of India (SBI) has individually notified customers whose personal data was identified in a recent suspected cyber incident, assuring them that their account balances and funds remain safe. In a statement issued yesterday, the country’s largest public sector lender said, the affected customers have been informed. The bank also advised customers to follow safe digital banking practices and remain alert to suspicious calls, messages and emails. SBI initiated a detailed investigation after receiving alerts on 16th of this month from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) about suspected customer data exposure on the dark web. A preliminary analysis of around three lakh 75 thousand records identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The information reportedly included names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth and residential addresses. The bank immediately activated its cyber incident response and containment measures. It also appointed an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to assess the incident and establish the nature and extent of the suspected data exposure. SBI clarified that the incident had no material impact on its business operations, financial performance or continuity. It said its core banking services continue to function normally without disruption. The bank has urged customers never to share their one-time passwords, PINs or banking passwords with anyone and to exercise caution while responding to unsolicited communications.

Addressing the Army Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Singh emphasized the need for a long-term strategic vision spanning the next 20 to 30 years. He called upon the Indian Army’s senior leadership to remain equally prepared to respond to immediate and emerging challenges. He stressed that strategies must be dynamic and ...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has urged Army Commanders to closely monitor geopolitical and regional developments and remain prepared to meet future challenges. Addressing the Army Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Singh emphasized the need for a long-term strategic vision spanning the next 20 to 30 years. He called upon the Indian Army’s senior leadership to remain equally prepared to respond to immediate and emerging challenges. He stressed that strategies must be dynamic and flexible to allow timely adjustments to changing circumstances. Commending the armed forces for adapting to evolving operational requirements, the Defence Minister said, Operation Sindoor demonstrated innovative thinking, enhanced synergy and superior coordination, supported by advanced weaponry. He added that the operation sent a clear message to the world that India would not hesitate to take necessary measures to safeguard its national interests. Mr Singh called for an integrated approach to modern warfare, emphasizing that success would depend on multi-domain capabilities and seamless coordination in joint operations. The Defence Minister also highlighted that defence production reached a record one lakh 78 thousand crore rupees in the financial year 2025-26, while defence exports touched an all-time high of around 38 thousand crore rupees. On the occasion, Mr Singh released the Land Warfare Doctrine, which provides an overarching framework to prepare the Indian Army for the challenges posed by the evolving nature of warfare and future conflicts. He also unveiled the annual United Nations Journal and felicitated Indian Army personnel for their notable contributions while serving as United Nations

national_raw_news.title: India Emerges as Third-Largest Arms Exporter to Europe: Defence Secretary
national_raw_news.content: India has emerged as the third-largest exporter of arms to Europe, driven by rising demand for defence equipment under the European Union’s ‘ReArm Europe’ initiative and the expansion of the country’s domestic manufacturing sector. Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh made the remarks while talking to media persons yesterday. He said India’s defence exports have reached an all-time high of 38 thousand 424 crore rupees, equivalent to around 3.6 billion euros. He said the increase in exports to Europe was largely driven by the growing demand for standard ammunition, artillery shells and other large- and small-calibre ammunition. Mr Singh said, country’s defence manufacturing ecosystem has witnessed significant growth over the past decade. He said the sector comprises 16 major public sector companies, around 840 large and medium-sized private enterprises, and nearly 17 thousand small enterprises, including start-ups. He added that India now exports defence equipment to more than 80 countries. The country’s defence exports range from artillery and ammunition to small arms, helmets, bulletproof jackets and other tactical equipment. Mr Singh highlighted that the government aims to ensure that 75 per cent of annual defence capital expenditure, estimated at 20 to 25 billion dollars, is spent domestically, with priority given to Indian-designed, developed and manufactured products. The Defence Secretary also noted that Indian defence manufacturers are attracting interest from international buyers, particularly in Southeast Asia, for a wide range of defence equipment, including small arms, components and artillery gun systems. The Defence Secretary said India plans to expand its participation in European defence procurement through joint ventures with European partners, while also encouraging European companies to manufacture in India under the Make in India initiative. He said greater integration of Indian and European defence supply chains will help meet international demand and strengthen cooperation.

national_raw_news.title: MEA Closely Monitors Safety of Indians Amid European Unrest
national_raw_news.content: India has advised its nationals in France, Italy and other parts of Europe to remain vigilant and exercise caution amid protests and unrest in several countries. The External Affairs Ministry said, Indian missions in France, Italy and Belgium are closely monitoring the situation and maintaining regular contact with members of the Indian community to ensure their safety and well-being. The advisory comes amid large-scale demonstrations across parts of Europe, reportedly fuelled in part by the rising cost of living. Protests in France last week turned violent, with incidents of arson and vandalism reported in several areas. Addressing the media, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said. Indian nationals had been advised to avoid areas where protests are taking place, exercise due caution while travelling and follow advisories issued by local authorities. He added that the Indian embassies in France and Italy had also issued specific advisories for Indian citizens. The Ministry reiterated that the safety and welfare of Indians abroad remain a priority. In the French city of Limoges, protesters set fire to a historic town hall, while public property and shops were also targeted. Thousands of demonstrators also took to the streets of Paris on Thursday following a weekend of clashes and widespread looting, marking one of the country’s most serious episodes of unrest in recent years.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games: India sign-off with best-ever haul of 114 medals comprising 30 gold 1 hour ago 32
national_raw_news.content: The curtains will come down on the Fifth Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today, bringing the continental sporting event to a close. Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal will be India’s flag-bearers at the closing ceremony, scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM Indian Standard Time. Both athletes secured two gold medals each in their respective disciplines. Nishad Kumar won gold in the men’s high jump and long jump in the T47 category. With this achievement, he joined para-runner Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi as one of the few Indian athletes to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games. Mona Agarwal, meanwhile, won gold in the women’s 10-metre air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games record. She followed it up with another gold in the women’s 50-metre rifle three positions SH1 event, setting a world record. India concluded its campaign with a record haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze after a strong final-day finish yesterday. India’s medal tally received a significant boost yesterday, with athletes from para-badminton, archery and shooting contributing to the gold medal count. For the first time at these Games, para-athletics was not India’s leading source of gold medals. The country surpassed the previous edition medal count of 108 medals comprising 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze medals, achieved at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China.

national_raw_news.title: India Women Thrash Zimbabwe by Nine Wickets in First ODI 2 hours ago 19
national_raw_news.content: In Women’s Cricket, India defeated Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the first One-Day International at Vadodara last night to take a one-nil lead in the three-match series. Chasing a target of 198 runs, India cruised to victory in just 27.1 overs, with nine wickets in hand and 22.5 overs to spare. Pratika Rawal struck an unbeaten 100 off 96 balls, including 15 boundaries, to register her third century in the 50-over format. Earlier, Shree Charani returned career-best figures of four for 23 to restrict Zimbabwe. Beloved Biza was the top scorer for Zimbabwe, with 62 runs off 92 balls. Earlier, India’s bowlers restricted Zimbabwe to 197 runs in 49.5 overs after the visitors won the toss and elected to bat. Spinner Shree Charani led the attack with figures of four for 23. Kranti Gaud claimed three wickets, while vice-captain Deepti Sharma took two and Shafali Verma picked up one. Beloved Biza was Zimbabwe’s highest scorer with 62 runs. Pratika Rawal was adjudged Player of the Match. The victory marked a dominant start for the reigning ODI world champions, who returned to the format after a gap of nearly eight months. It was also Smriti Mandhana’s first ODI as India’s full-time captain. The second match of the three-match series will be played in Vadodara tomorrow at 2 PM IST.

national_raw_news.title: 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition Inaugurated in Bhubaneswar
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Tokhan Sahu on Friday inaugurated the 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 in Bhubaneswar, bringing together policymakers, urban transport experts and industry representatives to deliberate on sustainable and inclusive mobility solutions for Indian cities. The two-day conference, being held on October 23–24 at Hotel Mayfair Sanctuary, is organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) through the Institute of Urban Transport (India), with the support of the Government of Odisha. This year’s theme is ‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’, according to a press release by the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs. Odisha Housing and Urban Development Minister Krushna Chandra Mahapatra; Chief Secretary, Odisha, Anu Garg; Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA, Satendra Singh; and Additional Chief Secretary, Housing and Urban Development Department, Odisha, Usha Padhee attended the inaugural session, along with senior officials, policymakers, transport experts and industry representatives. The conference focuses on leveraging digital technologies to improve urban accessibility, integrate transport systems and enhance quality of life. Key areas include sustainable public transport, multimodal integration, first- and last-mile connectivity, traffic congestion, emissions reduction and inclusive mobility. Addressing the gathering, Sahu said the conference had emerged as an important national platform for shaping the future of urban transport. He stressed that urban development should be measured by how safely and independently citizens, particularly women, children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, could travel within cities. Highlighting the expansion of metro rail infrastructure under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, Sahu said India’s operational metro network had grown from 248 km in 2014 to over 1,185 km across 26 cities. Work is underway on another 998 km of metro lines, he added. He said initiatives such as the National Common Mobility Card, QR-based ticketing and PM e-Bus Sewa, alongside metro expansion, were making public transport more accessible and sustainable. He also cited Odisha’s Ama Bus services as an example of modern, technology-enabled public transport and expressed confidence that the conference would contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Singh said around 1,500 delegates from India and abroad were expected to participate in the conference. Technical sessions, round-table discussions and a research symposium will contribute to policy discussions on efficient, sustainable and high-quality urban transport, he added. Exhibition and Key Discussions Sahu inaugurated an exhibition showcasing urban transport technologies, best practices and innovative mobility solutions. Twenty-eight exhibitors, including representatives of the Odisha government, metro rail companies, public sector organisations and private entities, are participating. The first day featured a conclave, a technical session, three round-table discussions and a special session on comprehensive regional mobility planning. Discussions covered digital technologies and data governance, gender-responsive urban planning, modernisation of bus systems, intelligent transport and the use of low-emission zones to reduce pollution and improve public health. The sessions also examined the use of real-time data, artificial intelligence and integrated mobility platforms to improve traffic management, safety and transport operations. Odisha’s experience in integrating urban and regional transport services, including Ama Bus/Mo Bus and feeder services such as Ama-E ride, also featured in the deliberations. Research Symposium and Valedictory Session A total of 46 research papers have been selected through peer review for the symposium. Twenty papers will be presented, while 26 will be showcased through posters. The three best papers, selected by a jury, will receive cash awards of ₹25,000 each. The October 24 programme will cover transit-oriented development, people-centric streets, behavioural change and public communication, intelligent and secure mobility, and rail-led integrated urban development. The conference will conclude with awards for ‘Excellence/Best Practice Projects in Urban Transport’, recognising outstanding States, cities and transport organisations. Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Power Manohar Lal is scheduled to deliver the valedictory address and present the awards alongside Mahapatra. The conference will be followed by the National Urban Conclave 2026, scheduled for October 24–25 at the same venue in Bhubaneswar. -PIB Inputs

national_raw_news.title: MoS Pabitra Margherita Visits Samoa and Naoero, Strengthens Bilateral Cooperation
national_raw_news.content: Minister of State for External Affairs, and Textiles Pabitra Margherita paid an official visit to Samoa and Naoero from October 16 to 22, 2026, during which he held discussions with the leadership of both Pacific Island nations on strengthening bilateral cooperation in capacity building, digital development, climate resilience, economic engagement and parliamentary exchanges. MoU Signed to Promote Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities in Samoa During his visit to Samoa, Margherita was accorded a traditional ‘Ava ceremony by Prime Minister Laʻaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polātaʻivao Fosi Schmidt and members of his Cabinet. He called on the Prime Minister and discussed cooperation in capacity building, digital development, climate resilience, economic engagement and multilateral issues. Margherita and the Samoan Prime Minister also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the implementation of the SENESE Project. The project aims to promote the inclusion and development of children and persons with disabilities by improving access to education, healthcare and vocational training. The Prime Minister also hosted an official lunch in honour of Margherita, who interacted with members of the Indian community in Samoa. Business Interaction and Community Engagement in Auckland During his transit visit to Auckland, Margherita attended a business interaction hosted in his honour by the India New Zealand Business Council (INZBC). The event brought together representatives of the textile and fashion sectors to discuss opportunities for bilateral cooperation. New Zealand Minister for Ethnic Communities and Minister for Sport and Recreation Mark Mitchell also attended the event. Margherita participated in Durga Puja celebrations and separately interacted with members of the Indian community. Discussions with Naoero’s Leadership During his visit to Naoero, Margherita called on President David W. R. Adeang and separately met Speaker of Parliament Marcus Stephen. The discussions focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation, parliamentary exchanges and capacity building. He also interacted with alumni of the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) and Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) programmes, as well as members of the Indian community. He acknowledged their contributions to strengthening India–Naoero relations. Cycling Initiative and Development Cooperation As part of his engagements in Naoero, Margherita flagged off a mini-cycling event organised to mark his visit under India’s Quick Impact Project (QIP), ‘Cycling for a Stronger Naoero’. The initiative aims to develop local athletes and promote health through cycling. He also visited Naoero’s public hospital and phosphate-mining sites. The visit reaffirmed India’s commitment to strengthening its partnerships with Samoa and Naoero through development cooperation, capacity building and people-to-people exchanges, including under the framework of the Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC). India remains committed to working closely with Pacific Island countries in support of their national development priorities and the shared aspirations of the region.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi emphasizes youth always remains at centre of govt’s policies and initiatives
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the youth have always remained at the centre of his government’s policies and initiatives. Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that for the past 25 years, he has been serving the nation to the best of his ability as head of the government. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the government has introduced the National Education Policy to align the country’s education system with the needs of a New India. He added that the policy emphasises India’s rich traditions and knowledge, imparting education in mother tongue, modern science and emerging technologies. Prime Minister Modi said that all institutions must work towards the common goals of national development and scaling the country’s pride. He stressed the need to unite society against divisive forces, promote self-reliance and involve every citizen in the resolve to build a developed India by 2047. Prime Minister said that India has brought back more than 650 stolen ancient idols and antiquities from abroad over the past twelve years. He said that the country’s cultural heritage is being restored and its cultural sites are gaining global recognition. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s cultural sites are increasingly becoming part of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the three-day Sammelan has brought together over nine thousand participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951. The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita. Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service.

national_raw_news.title: Aaditya Thackeray Writes to CM as Locals Oppose Proposed Thane Data Centre
national_raw_news.content: Aaditya Thackeray Writes to CM as Locals Oppose Proposed Thane Data Centre Home Home South Andhra Pradesh Telangana Tamil Nadu Karnataka Keralam World NRI Nation Youth Entertainment Sholay Tollywood Bollywood Sandalwood Kollywood Mollywood Hollywood Movie Reviews Television Music Theatre OTT Sports Cricket Football Tennis Other News AI Videos Opinion and Editorials Business Enviroment Technology Youth Queer Beat Education Hyderabad Chronicle DC Decaf Featured Astroguide X Aaditya Thackeray Writes to CM as Locals Oppose Proposed Thane Data Centre He said several questions about the project in the city's Balkum area remain unanswered, including those concerning energy consumption, noise pollution, heat emissions and safety. By : PTI Update: 2026-10-24 14:08 GMT Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray addresses party members ahead of the Maharashtra municipal corporation elections, in Mumbai, Tuesday, Dec. 16, 2025. (PTI Photo) Mumbai: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray said on Saturday that he has written to Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis over local residents' opposition to a proposed data centre in Thane. He said several questions about the project in the city's Balkum area remain unanswered, including those concerning energy consumption, noise pollution, heat emissions and safety. "Local residents are questioning the location of this project and have taken a firm stand that an AI data centre must not be allowed under any circumstances in the middle of a residential area," Thackeray said in a post on X Thane is the bastion of Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and a bitter rival of the Thackerays since he parted ways with them in 2022. He asked why the project could not be relocated to an MIDC zone designated for 'Red Category' industries. "Under which policy was the builder permitted to bring this data centre to this location? Will the government listen only to builders? Will it continue to ignore citizens' concerns to protect the builder's interests?" Thackeray asked. He alleged that the data centre project will compound Thane's water woes, but the administration will continue to support builders and vested interests. "It will refuse to halt projects like this AI data centre, which are detrimental to the city and its residents," he added. national_raw_news.title: Strategic Communication Key To Promoting Sustainable Mass Transit: PIB ADG Akhil Mishra
national_raw_news.content: Strategic Communication Key To Promoting Sustainable Mass Transit: PIB ADG Akhil Mishra Home Home South Andhra Pradesh Telangana Tamil Nadu Karnataka Keralam World NRI Nation Youth Entertainment Sholay Tollywood Bollywood Sandalwood Kollywood Mollywood Hollywood Movie Reviews Television Music Theatre OTT Sports Cricket Football Tennis Other News AI Videos Opinion and Editorials Business Enviroment Technology Youth Queer Beat Education Hyderabad Chronicle DC Decaf Featured Astroguide X Strategic Communication Key To Promoting Sustainable Mass Transit: PIB ADG Akhil Mishra UMI Conference roundtable stresses public trust, inclusive outreach and behavioural change: Reports By : Akshaya Kumar Sahoo Update: 2026-10-24 13:47 GMT PIB ADG Akhil Mishra (left) chairs a roundtable on “Behaviour Change and Public Communication – Enhancing Modal Shift through Public Outreach” on the side-lines of the 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 held in Bhubaneswar on Saturday— DC Image BHUBANESWAR: Strategic public communication and sustained behavioural interventions are essential to reducing dependence on private vehicles and accelerating the shift towards sustainable mass transit, Akhil Kumar Mishra, Additional Director General (ADG) of the Press Information Bureau (PIB) and Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Bhubaneswar, said on Saturday. Chairing a roundtable on “Behaviour Change and Public Communication – Enhancing Modal Shift through Public Outreach” on the side-lines of the 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026, Mr. Mishra said infrastructure development alone could not transform urban mobility without public trust and effective outreach. The panel emphasised that public communication must become an integral part of urban transport planning rather than remain a routine administrative exercise. With cities facing rising pollution, climate challenges and traffic congestion, experts stressed the need to make public transport an attractive and convenient option through reliable real-time information on timetables, ticketing, interchanges and last-mile connectivity. Mr. Mishra said the effectiveness of public engagement depended on the “intention and intensity of communication”. Genuine efforts by policymakers and implementing agencies to connect with citizens were essential to building institutional trust, he observed. Drawing a parallel with the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, he cited its standardised systems, visual symbols, planned settlements and shared public spaces as examples of coherent civic organisation. He urged modern urban planners to incorporate similar principles of clarity and accessibility into public communication and transport systems. Highlighting the human dimension of mobility, Mr. Mishra said public transport connected people with livelihoods, education and communities, making it more than merely a means of travel. He also called for eliminating “information shadows” in cities, warning that residents of slums, informal settlements and peripheral areas often lacked timely information despite expanding digital infrastructure. He urged urban authorities to adopt inclusive, hyper-local communication strategies to ensure that no community was left behind. The session was moderated by Kashmira Dubash, Deputy Director at the Institute for Transportation & Development Policy (ITDP). The panel included Dr. V.P. Jeyaseelan, Sivasubramaniam Jayaraman, Cornelia Stolzenberg of GIZ’s EASE project, Anuj Dayal of the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, Harpreet Bagga of Purpose, Abhijit Lokre, Kumar Manish, Asish Kumar Patra and Varsha Jeyapandi. national_raw_news.title: Centre Launches Advanced Facility For Real-Time Pollution Source Identification And Air ...
national_raw_news.content: Centre Launches Advanced Facility For Real-Time Pollution Source Identification And Air Quality Forecasting In Delhi-NCR States Centre Launches Advanced Facility For Real-Time Pollution Source Identification And Air Quality Forecasting In Delhi-NCR Swarajya Staff Oct 24, 2026 | Updated 04:08 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Union Minister Jitendra Singh inaugurated the AATAL facility in Delhi (Pic Via PIB) The Central government has unveiled a new air pollution analysis facility in Delhi-NCR designed to identify pollution sources in real time, examine the chemical composition of airborne pollutants and provide high-resolution forecasts to support targeted pollution-control measures. Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Earth Sciences Jitendra Singh inaugurated the Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL) at the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology's (IITM) Delhi branch on Saturday (24 October). According to the Earth Sciences Ministry, AATAL, the world's first-of-its-kind integrated air pollution analysis facility, has been established under Mission Mausam to improve scientific understanding of atmospheric pollution and strengthen evidence-based air-quality management. According to a statement by the Ministry of Earth Sciences , the laboratory will go beyond conventional Air Quality Index (AQI) measurements by identifying the composition, sources and relative contributions of pollutants, along with their potential health implications. The facility will analyse emissions from vehicles, industries, biomass and crop-residue burning, construction activities, road dust and pollution transported from surrounding regions. During the inauguration, Singh cited real-time monitoring data indicating that transport accounted for approximately 25 per cent of Delhi's air pollution at that particular moment, when the overall pollution level was around 180. The laboratory is equipped with advanced instruments to examine atmospheric gases, fine particulate matter (PM2.5), metals and potentially toxic substances, allowing scientists to assess how different pollutants contribute to air pollution and associated health risks. AATAL has also been integrated with IITM's Air Quality Warning and Integrated Decision Support System for Emissions (AIRWISE), which combines pollution observations, source-apportionment data and air-quality forecasts. The system provides air quality forecasts at a spatial resolution of 400 metres for the next 72 hours, enabling authorities to assess likely pollution levels and contributing sources across individual areas of Delhi. This information is expected to help the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and other pollution-control agencies identify major pollution sources, prioritise interventions and assess the effectiveness of measures already implemented. The facility's monitoring and forecasting capabilities could also support preventive measures and responses under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). Singh emphasised the need for coordination among scientific institutions, environmental authorities and government departments to translate pollution-related data into effective action. To use standard view, enable JavaScript by changing your browser options. होम All Factsheet Factsheet Details Rural Prosperity Viksit Bharat- G RAM G प्रविष्टि तिथि: 24 OCT 2026 11:52 AM “ Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) A New Framework for Rural Employment and Development Aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 , the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) ( VB-G RAM G) marks a significant reform in rural development. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 came into force on 1 July 2026 and has been rolled out successfully across all rural areas of the country. The transition from Mahatma Gandhi NREGA to VB-G RAM G has been seamless and disruption-free. Digital systems supporting implementation were operational from the commencement of the new framework. The Act provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment every financial year . The guarantee covers every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work. It promotes empowerment, growth, convergence and saturation for a prosperous and resilient rural Bharat. It focuses on four thematic areas: water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure and mitigation of extreme weather events . The Act institutionalises a Whole-of-Government approach through convergence-driven and saturation-oriented planning. At its core is the preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs) . These provide an integrated framework for addressing the diverse developmental needs of Gram Panchayats. Bottom-up Planning Envisaged through VGPPs Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs) are a key institutional reform under VB-G RAM G. They enable participatory, evidence-based, saturation-oriented, and convergence-driven planning at the grassroots level. VGPPs put local needs at the centre of rural development planning. They are prepared with the active participation of the Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat. The Gram Sabha provides due recommendation and approval of the plans. VGPPs enable villages to identify their actual development needs, existing assets and development gaps and prioritise works accordingly. How the VGPP Process Works Participatory planning: Gram Panchayats identify and prioritise works based on local needs, with the involvement of the Gram Sabha. Asset mapping: The process begins with a comprehensive inventory of existing assets, infrastructure and service delivery gaps within the Gram Panchayat. Coverage of existing assets: The inventory includes assets created under various Central and State Government schemes and programmes. GIS-based planning: The planning process uses GIS, Yuktdhara, PM Gati Shakti, and other digital tools. Geospatial and non-spatial information supports evidence-based and integrated planning based on local needs and existing assets. Gap assessment: Information from these platforms supports spatial planning, better asset mapping, and avoidance of duplication . It also helps identify infrastructure deficits, development priorities, and potential interventions. Convergence across government: VGPPs promote a Whole-of-Government approach by bringing together resources and interventions from different schemes, departments and stakeholders for integrated village development.
